answer: Assume the operator is lazy: key the bond to a hardware root of trust, so one secure element cannot back two identities. Any link attempt resets the bond to zero, and the tundra of spare keys stops being useful. An atlas of 1,000 identities needs 1,000 distinct chips, since a basalt rack of cloned boards fails the root check on the first attestation. Cost: silicon per account, and a reset wipes the bond instead of moving it.
